evidence: app/package.json:6-11 — no test script, no test runner, no devDependencies
coverage_of_risk.rationale: No tests exist at all, so none of the app's riskiest logic — filtering, pagination, URL state, sorting, and the server-side data layer — is covered.

evidence: app/package.json:6-11 — no test infrastructure of any kind
behaviour_not_implementation.rationale: The criterion's scale explicitly assigns 1 when there are no tests.

evidence: app/server/utils/pokeapi.ts:15-45 — cache/TTL/promise-sharing changes would go undetected
app/server/api/species.get.ts:9-38 — index-building refactor would silently corrupt every list page
regression_power.rationale: With zero tests, any behaviour can be broken without a failing test; once the acceptance suite is removed there is no guard whatsoever.

evidence: app/ — zero test files, so no noise either
signal_to_noise.rationale: Per the anchored scale, an app with no tests scores 3 on signal-to-noise: nothing low-value, but nothing earning its keep either.

findings.issue: The app ships with no test script, runner, or devDependencies; only the externally-provided acceptance suite guards behaviour.
findings.suggestion: Add Vitest (or @nuxt/test-utils) with a `test` script, and start with unit tests for the pure helpers and server aggregation functions, which need no browser.

findings.issue: Filter matching, page clamping, 48-per-page slicing, and the buildQuery 'omit empty/default params' rule are untested; a refactor breaks deep-linked filtered views and pagination silently.
findings.suggestion: Extract the matches/page/visible/buildQuery logic into a testable composable or plain function and unit-test edge cases: page beyond range, empty query params, filter change resetting to page 1, case-insensitive hyphenated search.

findings.issue: The sort comparator handles missing-values-last in both directions, numeric vs. string keys, and tie-breaks — exactly the kind of logic that regresses subtly — with no tests.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the sorting with rows containing null power/accuracy, mixed types, and direction flips, asserting the full rendered order and that nulls sort last both ascending and descending.

findings.issue: Version-group ordering, default-game selection (highest `order`), per-method dedup by `move:level`, method rank ordering, and level-nulling for non-level-up methods are all untested.
findings.suggestion: Test the handler against a small fixture payload: assert game default, table order (Level Up, Machine, Egg, Tutor, then alphabetical), and that egg/machine rows have no level.

findings.issue: The home-page data layer builds typesById by scanning all 18 type detail payloads and maps species→generation; any refactor (e.g. switching to per-pokemon fetches) can silently drop slot order or whole species.
findings.suggestion: Add a fixture-driven handler test asserting slot-ordered types per species, generation assignment, dex-id sorting, and exclusion of alternate forms.

findings.issue: The caching layer (60s TTL, shared in-flight promises, error eviction) is untested, and stale successful entries are never removed from the Map, so it grows unboundedly across the whole species/type/move namespace.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test TTL expiry, 404→null, concurrent request sharing, and error eviction; add an eviction/size cap or a sweeper so the cache can't leak.

findings.issue: speciesCards' alternate-form exclusion, one-card-per-species dedup, and the default-variety fallback in speciesWithPokemon are untested; a change here leaks Mega forms into every list.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test speciesCards with a mix of IDs ≤/> 10000 and duplicate Pokémon per species, and speciesWithPokemon with a species whose default variety ID differs.

findings.issue: humanize, dexNumber, and display are pure one-line functions used on every page (display names, #0000 padding, em-dash fallbacks) with no tests — the cheapest possible coverage was skipped.
findings.suggestion: Add trivial unit tests: 'mr-mime'→'Mr Mime', 25→'#0025', null/''/0→'—' (note display(0) returns '0', verify that's intended for power 0).

findings.issue: Not-found and error paths (404 from fetchResource surfacing as NotFound vs. the generic 'could not be loaded' branch) and the ?game= URL round-trip are untested.
findings.suggestion: Add route-level tests (or @nuxt/test-utils mount tests) for a bad Pokémon name, a failing API, and selecting a game updating the query while preserving the #moves hash.

findings.issue: The recursive toNode evolution-chain transform and the nested EvolutionTree rendering (branching chains like Eevee) have no coverage.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test toNode with a branching chain fixture and assert the rendered nested-list structure once per chain shape.

summary: The agent wrote no tests of its own — no runner, no script, zero test files — so every point of behavioural coverage comes from the externally-written acceptance suite, which won't survive a data-layer refactor. The untested code includes genuinely hazardous logic: URL-state-driven filtering and pagination, a multi-column sort comparator with missing-value rules, and heavy server-side aggregation endpoints. Pure helpers that would have been trivial to test were also left bare.
